## Check your understanding

1. If the vocabulary contains $V$ tokens, how many components does the logit vector contain at one position?

<details>
<summary>Show answer</summary>

It contains $V$ components, one for each vocabulary token.

</details>

2. Why does a logit with value 8 not mean an 80% probability?

<details>
<summary>Show answer</summary>

A logit is an unnormalized real-valued score. It is neither bounded between 0 and 1 nor constrained to sum to one. A separate transformation is needed to obtain a probability distribution.

</details>

3. What does the argmax of a logit vector identify?

<details>
<summary>Show answer</summary>

It identifies the token with the highest score in that vector. By itself, it does not measure confidence or truth.

</details>

4. Compare $z=(2,1)$ and $z'=(102,101)$. The logits are much larger in the second vector. Is the softmax distribution different? Why?

<details>
<summary>Show answer</summary>

No. The second vector is obtained by adding the same constant (100) to every component. This offset cancels in the softmax formula, so both vectors produce the same distribution. The absolute level of logits therefore has no standalone meaning; their differences matter.

</details>

## From final states to the next-token distribution {#ex-final-state-to-next-token}

A toy causal GPT receives the unpadded prefix $(A,B)$. The final states entering the output head are $h_1=(\ln 2,0)$ and $h_2=(0,\ln 3)$. The vocabulary is $(A,B,C)$ and the output head has weight rows $w_A=(1,0)$, $w_B=(0,1)$, and $w_C=(0,0)$, with zero bias. At position $t$, candidate $i$ gets the score $h_t\cdot w_i$.

1. Compute the logits for both positions and give the shape of the resulting matrix.
2. Apply softmax to each row. Which axis is normalized, and what must the probabilities sum to at each position?
3. Which prefix conditions each distribution? Which distribution is used to predict the token after the full prefix $(A,B)$?

<details>
<summary>Show the worked answer</summary>

1. The logit matrix has shape $(2,3)$. Its rows are positions and its columns are vocabulary candidates. The rows are $(\ln 2,0,0)$ and $(0,\ln 3,0)$.
2. Softmax normalizes the vocabulary axis independently at each position. The resulting distributions are $(1/2,1/4,1/4)$ and $(1/5,3/5,1/5)$, each summing to $1$.
3. The first row gives $P(\cdot\mid A)$. It assigns probability $1/4$ to the observed token $B$. The second gives $P(\cdot\mid A,B)$. Decoding uses this distribution to extend the full prefix.

</details>
